pr_title: [Merged by Bors] - update system test example to include using events
pr_body:
# Objective

- Adds an example of testing systems that handle events. I had a hard time figuring out how to do it a couple days ago so figured an official example could be useful.
- Fixes #4936

## Solution

- Adds a `Score` resource and an `EnemyDied` event. An `update_score` system updates the score when a new event comes through. I'm not sure the example is great, as this probably isn't how you'd do it in a real game, but I didn't want to change the existing example too much.
pr_comments: I'm happy with this! I'd like to merge this before reviving #3839.

> You updated the tests to use an app instead of a stage, except for the test `spawn_enemy_using_input_resource`. Could you also update it?

i can, just wasn't sure if I should. you only need to use `App` if you're adding events, otherwise using `World` works. since the example previously used that, I assumed it was the `default` way to test and that using app is the exception. if that's not the case tho, lemme know.

> You also didn't test that the event is correctly sent by the system `despawn_dead_enemies`, this should probably be asserted in the test `did_despawn_enemy`

updated
In my experience, `App` is needed for all but the most trivial tests. Usually you'll want to be testing that your plugin performs some end-to-end behavior, which requires both a schedule and a world.

> i can, just wasn't sure if I should. you only need to use `App` if you're adding events, otherwise using `World` works. since the example previously used that, I assumed it was the `default` way to test and that using app is the exception. if that's not the case tho, lemme know.

There isn't really a "default way to test" yet... For now I would prefer consistency in the tests over showing how to do it in a simpler case that might not be that useful as @alice-i-cecile noted
